analysis.title: Global Fund Manager Survey: The Sixth Sense (October 2026)
key_insights: October FMS (survey period Oct 2-8, 2026, 185 panellists with $512bn AUM) shows investors bullish into the US midterms, no Fed hike expected and strong Q3 earnings. 161 participants with $453bn AUM answered the global questions.
Investors say a 10-year Treasury yield of about 5.9% would make them shift allocation from stocks to bonds. 37% say 6.0%, 19% say they are already at a level that prompts a shift, 14% say 6.5%.

Average cash level held at 3.9% of AUM, above the 3.5% low in the Aug'26 survey and well below the 4.8% high in Apr'25. The BofA FMS Cash Rule stays in 'sell' territory (sell when cash is at or below 4.0%).
The BofA Bull & Bear Indicator stays at 8.1, which is a sell signal (sell above 8.0). The broader FMS sentiment measure fell to 6.4 from 7.0, the least bullish since Jun'26.
Growth expectations turned negative for the first time in 4 months: net 4% expect a weaker economy, versus net 8% expecting a stronger one in September.
'Boom' expectations (above-trend growth and above-trend inflation) are at net 47%, the highest since Feb'22. 45% expect 'stagflation', 4% 'goldilocks', 2% 'stagnation'.
Soft/no/hard landing split: 50% 'no landing' (down from 55% in Sept, lowest since Jun'26), 40% soft landing, 6% hard landing.

Inflation expectations fell to the lowest since Jan'25: net 5% expect lower global CPI in 12 months. Bond yield pessimism is the lowest since May'25, with net 1% expecting higher long-term rates, down from 15% in Sept.
Net 21% expect global corporate earnings to rise 10% or more over the next 12 months, a 4-month low in that measure. The summary says 6 in 10 investors expect double-digit EPS growth next year.
Net 7% say dividend payout ratios are too low, the most since Dec'13. On cash use, 39% want balance sheets improved, 35% want cash returned to shareholders, 22% want more capital spending.
76% do not expect a Fed hike at the Oct 28 FOMC, 21% expect one. The meeting falls 6 days before the US midterm elections.

In a Democratic sweep, 32% expect bond yields up and stocks down (down from 44% in Sept), 22% yields and stocks both down (up from 19%), 18% yields down and stocks up (up from 13%), 11% yields and stocks both up.

Most crowded trade is long global semiconductors (45%, down from a peak of 82% in Jul'26), then short Treasuries (27%, up from 18%), long Magnificent 7 (16%), long US dollar (5%), long oil (3%), long global banks (3%).

Biggest tail risks: disorderly rise in bond yields (31%), AI bubble (23%), second wave of inflation (20%), hyperscaler credit event (11%), geopolitical conflict (9%), Democratic sweep in the midterms (5%).
Most likely source of a systemic credit event: AI hyperscaler capex (39%), government debt (28%), private credit (24%).
57% expect no AI hyperscaler capex cut in the next 6 months, but 30% now expect one, up from 14% last month. 45% think there will be an AI bubble in 2027, 42% do not.

Investors are net 37% overweight technology (30% last month), the most since Aug'20. They are net 34% underweight consumer discretionary (21% last month), the most since Jul'08, and net 22% underweight real estate, the most since Aug'24.
Bank allocation fell 21ppt m/m to net 13% overweight, the biggest monthly drop since Mar'23 and the lowest allocation since Apr'26.
Monthly allocation shifts: increases in bonds, Japan and UK equities, utilities. Reductions in banks, US equities, consumer discretionary.
Equity allocation is net 44% overweight (49% last month). Bond allocation is net 37% underweight (48% underweight last month), the biggest bond short-cover in a year. Cash is equal-weight.
Investors expect Brent oil at about $94/bbl at year-end '26. The summary says a drop in oil to below $80/bbl would be the Q4 bull surprise and an AI capex cut the bear surprise.
FMS contrarian trades per the report: long bonds, REITs, consumer discretionary and staples; short stocks, tech, banks and EM.
Investors are taking net 9% lower than normal risk levels (net 2% lower last month). The FMS Financial Market Stability Risks Indicator rose to -0.9 from -1.1, with 5 of 7 risk factors increasing.

tension_points.theme: equity bullishness vs bond yield risk
tension_points.bull_case: Investors expect boom conditions (net 47%), no Fed hike (76%), double-digit earnings growth, and are net 44% overweight equities and net 37% overweight tech.
tension_points.bear_case: A disorderly rise in bond yields is the top tail risk (31%). Cash at 3.9% and the Bull & Bear Indicator at 8.1 are both contrarian sell signals. 45% expect stagflation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The 10-year Treasury yield reaching about 5.9%-6.0%, the level at which investors say they would shift from stocks to bonds.

tension_points.bull_case: 57% expect no hyperscaler capex cut in the next 6 months, and investors are the most overweight tech since Aug'20.
tension_points.bear_case: 30% now expect a capex cut (up from 14%), 45% expect an AI bubble in 2027, and 39% see hyperscaler capex as the likeliest source of a systemic credit event.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An AI hyperscaler capex cut, which the report calls the bear surprise.

theme_stances.key_argument: Growing share of investors expect a hyperscaler capex cut, and AI capex is seen as the most likely source of a systemic credit event.
theme_stances.evidence: AI capex cut = the bear surprise

theme_stances.key_argument: Investors say a 10-year yield near 6% would flip allocation from stocks to bonds, and a disorderly rise in yields is the top tail risk.
theme_stances.evidence: waiting for ~6% yields before flipping from stocks to bonds
